propositions.name: aether_continuous_incompressible_medium
propositions.statement: The aether is a continuous, homogeneous, and incompressible medium endowed with inertia and with elasticity purely rotational.
propositions.quote: the æther to be a continuous, homogeneous, and incompressible medium, endowed with inertia and with elasticity purely rotational

propositions.name: electrons_as_point_singularities
propositions.statement: Electrons exist as point-singularities, or centres of intrinsic strain, in the medium, which can move about under their mutual actions.
propositions.quote: unitary electric charges, or electrons, exist as point-singularities, or centres of intrinsic strain, which can move about under their mutual actions

propositions.name: atoms_are_electron_aggregations
propositions.statement: Atoms of matter are in whole or in part aggregations of electrons in stable orbital motion.
propositions.quote: atoms of matter are in whole or in part aggregations of electrons in stable orbital motion

propositions.name: matter_theory_ultimately_atomic
propositions.statement: An adequate theory of material phenomena is necessarily ultimately atomic.
propositions.quote: An adequate theory of material phenomena is necessarily ultimately atomic.

propositions.name: actions_propagated_in_time
propositions.statement: Actions are propagated in time and space from one molecule of matter to the surrounding ones rather than acting instantaneously at a distance.
propositions.quote: actions are propagated in time and space from one molecule of matter to the surrounding ones in accordance with the system of mathematical equations

propositions.name: medium_requires_inertia_elasticity
propositions.statement: A medium must transmit actions across it in time, and therefore must be postulated to have inertia and elasticity.
propositions.quote: must transmit actions across it in time ; therefore there must be postulated for it the property of inertia

propositions.name: aether_fluid_form_elastic_rotation
propositions.statement: The aether has perfect fluidity as regards form, but elastic resistance to rotational displacement.
propositions.quote: there is perfect fluidity as regards form, but elastic resistance to rotational displacement

propositions.name: no_volume_elasticity_in_aether
propositions.statement: No phenomenon has been discovered that shows the property of elasticity of volume is present in the aether.
propositions.quote: no phenomenon has been discovered which would allow us to assume that the property of elasticity of volume, which necessarily exists in any molecularly constituted medium such as matter, is present in the æther at all

propositions.name: quiescent_aether_absolute_rest
propositions.statement: The spatial framework in absolute rest to which the dynamics of matter is referred is in fact the quiescent underlying aether.
propositions.quote: the spacial framework in absolute rest, which was introduced by Newton and was probably a main source of the great advance in abstract dynamics originated by the Principia , is in fact the quiescent underlying æther

propositions.name: high_inertia_elasticity_for_light_speed
propositions.statement: The medium is assumed to have a high coefficient of inertia and an extremely high elasticity in order to conserve the ascertained velocity of radiation.
propositions.quote: we have been compelled to assume a high coefficient of inertia of the medium, and therefore an extremely high elasticity in order to conserve the ascertained velocity of radiation

propositions.name: electron_pairs_positive_negative
propositions.statement: A positive electron and its complementary negative electron are formed together as conjugate point-singularities in the medium.
propositions.quote: A will be a positive electron in the medium, and B will be the complementary negative one.

propositions.name: electron_mutual_destruction_improbable
propositions.statement: Mutual destruction of two complementary electrons by direct impact is an occurrence of infinitely small probability.
propositions.quote: mutual destruction of two complementary electrons by direct impact is an occurrence of infinitely small probability

propositions.name: electrons_persist_until_destroyed
propositions.statement: Electrons can be moved about through the medium, but persist until they are destroyed by an extraneous process the reverse of that by which they are formed.
propositions.quote: each of them can be moved about through the medium, but they will both persist until they are destroyed by an extraneous process the reverse of that by which they are formed

propositions.name: strain_form_moves_without_medium
propositions.statement: A strain-form such as a doublet can be displaced into a different position at any distance without the medium moving along with it.
propositions.quote: it can be displaced into a different position, at any distance, as a strain-form, without the medium moving along with it

propositions.name: ponderomotive_force_charge_times_field
propositions.statement: For each electron at rest, the ponderomotive force is equal to its charge multiplied by the intensity of the electric field where it is situated.
propositions.quote: for each electron at rest, this force is equal to its charge multiplied by the intensity of the electric field where it is situated

propositions.name: contact_force_via_energy_function
propositions.statement: Transmission of force by contact action is explained by assigning the mathematical function representing the medium's energy of strain, from which stress is derived by the principle of virtual work.
propositions.quote: the scientific method of describing them is to assign the mathematical function which represents its energy of strain, and thence derive its relations of stress by the principle of virtual work

propositions.name: kinetic_energy_is_aethereal_energy
propositions.statement: The kinetic energy of matter is itself, in whole or in part, energy in the aether arising from the movement of the strain-forms across it.
propositions.quote: increasing the kinetic energy of the matter, which is itself, in whole or in part, energy in the æther arising from the movement of the strain-forms across it

propositions.name: forces_from_potential_energy_function
propositions.statement: The mutual forces of a steady system are derived from a single analytical function which is its available potential energy.
propositions.quote: the mutual forces of such a system are derived from a single analytical function which is its available potential energy

propositions.name: aether_not_matter_own_laws
propositions.statement: The aether, not being matter, need not obey the laws of the dynamics of matter, provided it obeys another scheme of dynamical laws consistent among themselves.
propositions.quote: The æther not being matter, it need not obey the laws of the dynamics of matter, provided it obey another scheme of dynamical laws consistent among themselves

propositions.name: aether_spatial_relations_incompressibility_rotation
propositions.statement: The spatial relations of the aether on which its dynamics depend are those of incompressibility and rotational elasticity.
propositions.quote: The sole spacial relations of the æther itself, on which its dynamics depend, those namely of incompressibility and rotational elasticity

propositions.name: molecular_movements_slow_equilibrium
propositions.statement: Molecular movements are usually so slow that the surrounding aether is at each instant practically in an equilibrium condition, so material atoms act on each other from a distance obeying definite laws.
propositions.quote: molecular movements so slow that the surrounding rather is at each instant practically in an equilibrium condition, so that the material atoms practically act on each other from a distance with forcives obeying definite laws

propositions.name: molecule_internal_energy_orbital_motions
propositions.statement: The energy of the steady orbital motions in the molecule makes up both the energy of chemical constitution and the internal thermal energy.
propositions.quote: the energy of the steady orbital motions in the molecule (including therein slow free precessions) makes up both the energy of chemical constitution and the internal thermal energy

propositions.name: temperature_no_spectral_line_shift
propositions.statement: Change of temperature has no influence on the positions of the lines in a spectrum.
propositions.quote: this explains why change of temperature has no influence on the positions of the lines in a spectrum

propositions.name: specific_heat_ratio_bounds
propositions.statement: The ratio of the specific heats in a gas must lie between 1 and a fixed upper bound.
propositions.quote: The ratio of the specific heats in a gas must still lie between 1 and

propositions.name: vacuum_jacket_insulates_heat
propositions.statement: A vacuum jacket has remarkable insulating power as regards heat.
propositions.quote: the remarkable insulating power of a vacuum jacket as regards heat

propositions.name: chemical_affinity_persists_low_temperature
propositions.statement: The energies of affinity exist at all temperatures in probably undiminished strength, while the forces of cohesion are modified by the fall of temperature but not necessarily toward extinction.
propositions.quote: the energies of affinity exist all the time in probably undiminished strength, while the forces of cohesion are modified by the fall of temperature but not necessarily in the direction of extinction

propositions.name: gravitation_not_statical_stress
propositions.statement: Gravitation cannot be transmitted by any action of the nature of statical stress, since the approach of two atoms would then increase the strain and the stress and cause the mutual forces to resist approach.
propositions.quote: gravitation cannot be transmitted by any action of the nature of statical stress; for then the approach of two atoms would increase the strain, and therefore also the stress

propositions.name: gravitation_isotropic_at_electrons
propositions.statement: Gravitation must belong to the ultimate constituents of matter, the electrons, and must be isotropic all round each of them.
propositions.quote: gravitation must belong to the ultimate constituents of matter, that is on this theory to the electrons, and must be isotropic all round each of them

propositions.name: maxwell_equations_verified_experiment
propositions.statement: Maxwell's equations of the electric field in free space form a sufficient description of the free aether and have been verified by experiment.
propositions.quote: they may be based directly on Maxwell 's equations of the electric field in free space , which form a sufficient description of the free æther, and have been verified by experiment

propositions.name: total_displacement_sum_polarization_aethereal
propositions.statement: The total circuital displacement of Maxwell's theory is the sum of the electric polarization of the material and the aethereal elastic displacement.
propositions.quote: let ( f', g', h') denote the electric polarization of the material, and ( f, g, h ) the æthereal elastic displacement, so that the total circuital displacement of Maxwell 's theory is their sum

propositions.name: electric_force_acts_on_electrons
propositions.statement: The electric force is that which acts on the electrons.
propositions.quote: let (P, Q, R) denote the electric force, namely that which acts on the electrons

propositions.name: aethereal_force_produces_aethereal_displacement
propositions.statement: The aethereal force is that which produces the aethereal electric displacement.
propositions.quote: (P', Q', R') the æthereal force, that which produces the æthereal electric displacement ( f, g, h )

propositions.name: migration_current_small
propositions.statement: The current of migration of the free electric charge is in all cases very small in comparison with the conducted part of the current.
propositions.quote: the current ( u 0 , v 0 , w 0 ) of migration of the free electric charge as this is in all cases very small in comparison

propositions.name: electrons_carried_by_matter_steady_state
propositions.statement: Viscous diffusion of momentum among moving ions and molecules leads to the electrons constituting electric densities being wholly carried on by the matter whenever a steady state is attained.
propositions.quote: viscous diffusion of momentum among moving ions and molecules, which produces Ohmic resistance to a steady current, will lead to the electrons constituting electric densities being wholly carried on by the matter whenever a steady state is attained

propositions.name: rowland_convection_currents_confirm
propositions.statement: The carrying of electric charge by moving matter is in keeping with Rowland's classical experiments on convection currents.
propositions.quote: This necessary consequence of the theory is in keeping with Rowland's classical experiments on convection currents.

propositions.name: convection_alone_no_charge_separation
propositions.statement: Mere convection of the polarized medium does not produce separation of free electricity.
propositions.quote: which asserts (for the case of uniform motion that is contemplated) that mere convection of the polarized medium does not produce separation of free electricity

propositions.name: fresnels_law_velocity_alteration
propositions.statement: The velocity of propagation of radiation in a moving material medium is altered according to Fresnel's law.
propositions.quote: which agrees with the equation obtained in Part I. §124 and Part II. §13, leading to Fresnel's law of alteration of the velocity of propagation

propositions.name: moving_body_contracts_direction_motion
propositions.statement: A body in uniform motion through the aether is shrunk in the direction of its velocity.
propositions.quote: one consequence of the motion thus being that the body is shrunk in the direction of its velocity v in the ratio

propositions.name: contraction_confirms_fitzgerald_lorentz
propositions.statement: If the argument for the shrinking of a moving body is valid, it confirms the hypothesis of FitzGerald and Lorentz, to which they were led as the ultimate resource for explaining the negative result of Michelson's optical experiments.
propositions.quote: it will confirm the hypothesis of FitzGerald and Lorentz , to which they were led as the ultimate resource for the explanation of the negative result of Michelson 's optical experiments

propositions.name: molecule_constitution_wholly_electric
propositions.statement: Confirmation of the contraction argument involves evidence that the constitution of a molecule is wholly electric.
propositions.quote: it will involve evidence that the constitution of a molecule is wholly electric, as here represented
